oidc_jwt.description: Reusing the same upstream JWT can succeed multiple times because Vault JWT auth is a stateless verifier and the docs do not describe jti tracking or one-time JWT consumption.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not report replay_same_token or missing jti tracking as a vulnerability for oidc_jwt by default.

oidc_jwt.description: JWT auth documentation does not describe jti tracking or one-time JWT consumption; replay of the same bearer JWT may therefore be accepted by design until token freshness constraints fail.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag replay_same_token as a vulnerability for stateless JWT verification absent explicit one-time semantics.

oidc_jwt.description: Vault token lookup-self display_name may include an auth mount-derived prefix before the upstream identity value.
oidc_jwt.source: Vault token lookup-self example shows ldap2-tesla
oidc_jwt.note: Prefix differences alone are not identity-collision bugs.

oidc_jwt.description: Vault OIDC provider advertises only public subject types.
oidc_jwt.note: Stable public subject identifiers across clients are by design for this provider configuration and should not be mistaken for pairwise-subject isolation failures.

oidc_jwt.description: Vault's OIDC provider advertises request_parameter_supported=false and request_uri_parameter_supported=false.
oidc_jwt.note: Unsigned request object tests are not applicable to this provider surface.

oidc_jwt.description: Vault's OIDC provider does not support request or request_uri parameters.
oidc_jwt.note: Unsigned request-object attacks are not applicable to this provider endpoint.

oidc_jwt.description: An OIDC provider with empty allowed_client_ids allows no clients.
oidc_jwt.note: Authorization failures in this state are expected configuration behavior, not over-restriction bugs.

oidc_jwt.description: Multiple authenticated entities can be bound to the same entity alias name, causing them to gain access to all privileges associated with that alias.
oidc_jwt.note: Alias collisions are explicitly warned about in the docs; tests should distinguish documented alias reuse risk from accidental platform bugs.

oidc_jwt.description: JWT login uses the auth mount's configured default_role when no role is provided.
oidc_jwt.note: Behavior changes after updating default_role are by design for new logins.

oidc_jwt.constraint: Exactly one of oidc_discovery_url, jwks_url, and jwt_validation_pubkeys must be set in configure_jwt_validation. The fuzzer MUST NOT send more than one trust source, or setup will be invalid.

bound_issuer is optional in configure_jwt_validation. For I1 issuer-validation tests (trust_anchor_substitution, jwt_bound_issuer_enforce), the fuzzer MUST explicitly set bound_issuer; otherwise Vault skips issuer comparison entirely.

bound_issuer cannot be configured when jwks_pairs is set. For issuer-enforcement tests, the fuzzer MUST use oidc_discovery_url, jwks_url, or jwt_validation_pubkeys instead of jwks_pairs if it needs bound_issuer.

Every JWT/OIDC role requires at least one bound value to be set. The fuzzer MUST configure at least one of bound_audiences, bound_subject, bound_claims, or other documented bound values, or role creation is invalid.

For role_type=jwt, bound_audiences is required when the JWT contains an aud claim (typical case) and must match at least one JWT aud value. For I5 audience tests, the control token MUST include a matching aud and the attack token MUST vary only aud.

bound_subject supports exact string match only; there is no companion type parameter. For I4 multi-identity tests, the fuzzer MUST OMIT bound_subject entirely if multiple different sub values need to authenticate to the same role. Setting bound_subject to '*' matches only the literal string '*'.

bound_claims keys support JSON pointer syntax, but matching mode is controlled only by bound_claims_type. If bound_claims_type='string' (default), values are treated as literals and must match exactly. For I4 multi-identity tests, exact-match bound_claims MUST be omitted rather than set to wildcard-like values unless bound_claims_type='glob' is explicitly set.
For I5 wildcard tests, bound_claims_type must be set to 'glob'. In the default 'string' mode, '*' is a literal character, not a wildcard.

bound_claims accepts string, integer, boolean, or list values. Because the default bound_claims_type='string' treats values as literals, the fuzzer SHOULD test numeric type coercion carefully. For I5 numeric coercion tests, set bound_claims_type='glob' so non-string JWT claim values are coerced to strings rather than rejected outright.
Numeric sentinel semantics: clock_skew_leeway value 0 means use default 60 seconds, not strict zero; value -1 disables extra leeway. Never assume 0 means no leeway.
Numeric sentinel semantics: expiration_leeway value 0 means use default 150 seconds, not strict zero; value -1 disables extra leeway. Never assume 0 means no leeway.
Numeric sentinel semantics: not_before_leeway value 0 means use default 150 seconds, not strict zero; value -1 disables extra leeway. Never assume 0 means no leeway.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests on JWT roles, the fuzzer MUST include a control login using a valid token (for example exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}}, iat={{now_epoch}}) alongside the attack login. Without a control, LOGIN_FAILED cannot be distinguished from broken trust/config setup.

token_num_uses limits every API call made with the resulting Vault session token, including verify_granted_identity and verify_read_secret. If the sequence performs both self-lookup and secret-read, the minimum safe token_num_uses is 2; use 3+ if additional session-inspection calls are present.
oidc_jwt.source: tokenfields behavior reflected in Vault token lookup docs and fuzzer execution context

oidc_jwt.constraint: JWT bearer replay of the same upstream JWT is not documented as prevented by Vault JWT login. The fuzzer MUST treat replay_same_token and stateless_jwt_no_jti as hardening-only for oidc_jwt, not as vulnerabilities, unless a separate one-time assertion context is being tested.
oidc_jwt.source: JWT auth docs plus RFC7519 replay model

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I3 jwt_signing_key_rotation tests, the fuzzer MUST re-run login after updating configure_jwt_validation trust material. A successful baseline login before rotation does not imply stale-cache behavior; only a post-rotation login with the old key demonstrates coherence failure.

For I3 jwt_default_role_change tests, login_with_jwt may omit role and then uses default_role from mount config. The fuzzer MUST ensure the role parameter is omitted, not sent with the old role, when testing default_role changes.

For I3 config-change sequences, NEW logins evaluated under updated role or mount config are by design. A valid coherence test must compare behavior of the same JWT before and after config change, not treat admin reconfiguration itself as a bug.

user_claim becomes the identity entity alias name and must resolve to a string. For I4 principal-binding tests, the fuzzer should vary the claim selected by user_claim (commonly sub) and compare resulting entity IDs and aliases; non-string claim values are invalid setup, not collisions.

groups_claim must resolve to a list of strings. For I4 type_confusion_groups tests, sending groups as a bare string may be rejected as invalid rather than mapped differently; the fuzzer must distinguish schema rejection from identity-collision behavior.

OIDC provider client assignments default to allowing no Vault entities. When creating an OIDC client under /identity/oidc/client, the fuzzer MUST set assignments appropriately (for example allow_all or a matching assignment) or authorization flow tests will fail due to client assignment denial, not security enforcement.

OIDC provider allowed_client_ids on the provider defaults to allowing no clients when empty. The fuzzer MUST configure allowed_client_ids or '*' on the provider before testing provider authorize/token/userinfo flows.

For Vault OIDC provider flows, redirect_uris on the client must exactly match the redirect_uri used in authorization and token requests. The fuzzer MUST use byte-for-byte identical redirect_uri values in start_oidc_auth and exchange_code_for_token.
oidc_jwt.source: identity/oidc client and token endpoint docs

oidc_jwt.constraint: Public OIDC clients must use PKCE and confidential clients may use PKCE. For tests involving public clients, the fuzzer MUST send code_challenge at authorize time and code_verifier at token time; omission causes expected flow rejection, not a vulnerability.

Vault OIDC provider discovery advertises request_parameter_supported=false and request_uri_parameter_supported=false. The fuzzer MUST NOT run oidc_request_object_alg_none against Vault's provider endpoints because request objects are not supported there; such a test would be invalid setup.

The UserInfo endpoint documentation text says POST but the sample request uses GET. Treat this as documentation inconsistency; for sequence stability, prefer the documented protected-resource semantics and verify identity using Vault token lookup-self instead of relying on provider userinfo method ambiguity.
KV v2 reads must use the /data/ path segment. The fuzzer MUST use /v1/{engine}/data/{path} for verify_read_secret on KV v2 mounts; omitting /data/ will hit the wrong API shape and produce false 404s.

KV v2 list operations require permissions on /metadata/ paths even if reads/writes use /data/. If the fuzzer seeds or verifies resources on KV v2, policies must grant the appropriate capabilities on both /data/ and /metadata/ paths as needed, or failures may be policy-shape artifacts.

KV v2 engine config sentinel: max_versions value 0 means keep the default 10 versions, not zero versions. delete_version_after value '0s' means no automatic deletion. Never assume zero disables storage or means immediate deletion.

Global group policy application mode affects whether identity group policies apply only within namespace hierarchy or across any namespace. For I5 group_policy_escalation tests, the fuzzer MUST account for /sys/config/group-policy-application because mode='any' can legitimately broaden cross-namespace group policy application by design.
JWT/OIDC auth config requires exactly one trust source: set ONE AND ONLY ONE of oidc_discovery_url, jwks_url, or jwt_validation_pubkeys. Do not combine them, or setup is invalid.

For I1 issuer-validation tests, configure_jwt_validation MUST include bound_issuer unless intentionally testing the unbound case. If bound_issuer is omitted, Vault will not compare the JWT iss claim, so issuer-substitution tests become meaningless.
When jwks_pairs is configured, bound_issuer cannot be configured. Do not attempt issuer-binding tests with jwks_pairs; use jwks_url, oidc_discovery_url, or jwt_validation_pubkeys instead.

Every JWT/OIDC role must have at least one bound value set. The fuzzer MUST configure at least one constraint such as bound_audiences, bound_subject, bound_claims, or equivalent role restriction; otherwise role creation/update is invalid.

For JWT roles that contain an aud claim (typical case), bound_audiences is required and must match at least one JWT aud value. For I5 audience tests, include a control token whose aud matches the configured bound_audiences; otherwise rejection may be due to missing required audience binding rather than the attack mutation.

bound_subject supports EXACT string match only. There is no companion type parameter for bound_subject. Wildcards like '*' are treated literally, not as patterns. For I4 multi-identity tests, OMIT bound_subject entirely rather than setting it to '*'.

bound_claims supports two matching modes controlled by bound_claims_type. Default bound_claims_type='string' means literal exact matching; 'glob' enables wildcard matching with '*'. For I4 multi-identity scenarios that need multiple distinct values to pass the same role, either omit the constrained claim or explicitly use bound_claims_type='glob'; do NOT set bound_claims values to '*' while leaving the default string mode.

bound_claims values may be string, integer, boolean, or list of strings. Because the default bound_claims_type='string' treats values as literals with exact matching, the fuzzer SHOULD test numeric type coercion explicitly. For I5 numeric coercion tests, set bound_claims_type='glob' so non-string JWT claim values are coerced to strings for matching rather than being rejected outright by strict literal handling.

user_claim must resolve to a STRING value and becomes the identity entity alias name on successful login. For I4 principal-binding tests, vary the actual string value of the configured user_claim and compare resulting aliases/entities; non-string claim values are invalid setup, not security findings.

groups_claim must resolve to a LIST OF STRINGS. Sending a scalar string where a list is required is invalid setup. For I4/I5 group-mapping tests, distinguish type-rejection from alias-collision behavior.

Numeric sentinel semantics for JWT leeway fields: clock_skew_leeway value 0 means use default 60 seconds, not strict zero; value -1 disables added leeway. expiration_leeway value 0 means use default 150 seconds, not strict zero; value -1 disables added leeway. not_before_leeway value 0 means use default 150 seconds, not strict zero; value -1 disables added leeway. Never assume 0 means no leeway.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests, include a CONTROL login using a valid token alongside the attack token. Vault's default leeway is nonzero unless explicitly disabled with -1, so near-boundary timestamps may still pass. Use {{now_epoch_plus_N}} / {{now_epoch_minus_N}} values far beyond configured leeway, or set expiration_leeway and not_before_leeway to -1 for strict tests.

token_num_uses limits total uses of the issued Vault token, and EVERY authenticated API call consumes uses, including verify_granted_identity and verify_read_secret. If the sequence performs both self-lookup and secret-read, minimum safe token_num_uses is 2; use 3+ if additional session-bound verification calls are present. Setting token_num_uses=1 will exhaust the token before the access test and cause misleading failures.

OIDC auth_url and callback are session-bound by state, nonce, and optional client_nonce. For I3 flow-coherence tests, preserve the exact state/nonce pair returned for a given auth_url request and do not mix them across sessions except when intentionally testing state-swap behavior.
oidc_jwt.source: auth/jwt OIDC authorization URL request + OIDC callback

oidc_jwt.constraint: If client_nonce is supplied to /auth/{mount}/oidc/auth_url, the SAME client_nonce must be supplied to /auth/{mount}/oidc/callback. Missing or mismatched client_nonce is invalid setup, not a security finding.
oidc_jwt.source: auth/jwt OIDC authorization URL request + OIDC callback

oidc_jwt.constraint: OIDC role allowed_redirect_uris is required for OIDC logins, and the redirect_uri used in the flow must be one of those exact configured values. For I3 redirect/callback tests, ensure the role and upstream client are both configured with the exact callback URI under test.

Vault JWT login defaults to the mount's default_role when role is omitted. For I3 default-role-change tests, omit the role parameter intentionally and verify behavior changes only after reconfiguring default_role; when testing a specific role, always send role explicitly to avoid accidental default-role binding.

Vault OIDC provider clients default to no allowed entities via assignments. A client with empty assignments allows no Vault entities to authenticate. To permit all entities in provider-side OIDC tests, supply the built-in allow_all assignment; otherwise authorization failures are expected setup behavior.
oidc_jwt.source: identity/oidc provider client Create or update a client

oidc_jwt.constraint: OIDC provider redirect_uris must exactly match the redirect_uri used in each authentication request. For provider-side OIDC flow tests, do not rely on prefix or wildcard matching; mismatches are by-design rejections.
oidc_jwt.source: identity/oidc provider client Create or update a client

oidc_jwt.constraint: OIDC provider public clients MUST use PKCE for the authorization code flow; confidential clients may use PKCE optionally. For tests involving public clients, include code_challenge at authorize time and code_verifier at token time, otherwise failures are expected.
oidc_jwt.source: identity/oidc provider client Create or update a client + provider authorize/token endpoints

oidc_jwt.constraint: Vault provider discovery explicitly reports request_parameter_supported=false and request_uri_parameter_supported=false. Do NOT run OIDC request-object or request_uri attack patterns against this provider endpoint; unsupported parameters are by design and would create false positives.

Vault provider discovery reports response_types_supported=['code'] and grant_types_supported=['authorization_code'] only. Do not test implicit, hybrid, or token-exchange grants against this provider token endpoint; unsupported grant failures are expected.

The provider token endpoint requires redirect_uri to exactly match the value used when the authorization code was generated. For I3 redirect_uri_mismatch tests, a mismatch should be evaluated as flow rejection, not identity confusion.

Provider token endpoint client authentication depends on client_type and auth method: public clients require client_id and code_verifier; confidential clients require either Authorization: Basic or client_id/client_secret for client_secret_post. Missing required client auth is invalid setup.

The UserInfo endpoint is a protected resource requiring Authorization: Bearer <access_token>. The fuzzer MUST treat access_token as the session credential for provider-side verification; id_token is not the bearer credential for /userinfo.

Identity group aliases require a mount_accessor and canonical group ID. The fuzzer MUST obtain the auth mount accessor for the JWT mount before creating group aliases; using the wrong accessor binds external groups to the wrong auth source and invalidates I4/I5 group tests.

External identity groups should be populated through aliases from auth methods. While the generic group API allows member_entity_ids/member_group_ids fields, group alias mapping is the documented mechanism for external JWT/OIDC groups. For group-policy escalation tests, prefer external groups plus group aliases over manually stuffing members into an external group.

Entity alias names are security-sensitive. Vault explicitly warns that multiple authenticated entities can be bound to the same alias and thereby share privileges. For I4 collision tests, alias reuse leading to privilege sharing is a documented risk surface, not a random artifact; ensure each test identity uses a unique alias value unless intentionally probing collisions.

Entity merge is an admin operation that can intentionally collapse identities, and merges fail when aliases share the same mount accessor unless conflicting_alias_ids_to_keep is provided and entities are merged one at a time. Do not interpret admin-driven merges as spontaneous I4 violations.

KV v2 engine config sentinel semantics: max_versions=0 does NOT mean keep zero versions; it means use the default of 10 versions. delete_version_after='0s' means no automatic deletion timer. Never assume zero disables storage or makes data immediately unavailable.

KV v2 list operations use the /metadata/ path, while reads and writes use /data/. For access tests, grant read on /data/{path} and list on /metadata/{path} separately if listing is needed. A 403 on /metadata/ is not evidence that /data/ access is denied.
For verify_read_secret on Vault KV v2, the path MUST include /data/. Using /{engine}/{path} instead of /{engine}/data/{path} hits the wrong API shape and causes false 404/permission results.

Vault's legacy policy endpoint /sys/policy is documented here, but policy updates take effect immediately for associated users. For I3 config-change tests involving authorization, re-login after policy changes and do not treat changed behavior under updated policy as stale-session inconsistency unless the same request is evaluated inconsistently without a legitimate config change.

Global group policy application mode can be 'within_namespace_hierarchy' or 'any'. In Enterprise environments, cross-namespace group policy effects depend on this setting. For I5 group-policy escalation tests, read or control this mode before concluding that cross-namespace policy application is excessive.

Exactly one global JWT trust source must be configured in configure_jwt_validation: oidc_discovery_url, jwks_url, or jwt_validation_pubkeys. jwks_pairs is also mutually exclusive with jwks_url/jwks_ca_pem, and bound_issuer cannot be configured when jwks_pairs is set. Do not build I1/I3 trust-anchor tests with multiple trust sources enabled at once.

Every JWT/OIDC role must have at least one bound value configured. The docs state at least one bound value must be set. A role with no bound constraints is invalid test setup and may fail creation or produce meaningless I5 results.

For JWT roles carrying an aud claim, bound_audiences is required and must match at least one JWT aud value. For I5 audience tests, include a control token whose aud matches the configured bound_audiences; otherwise a failed attack login may just reflect missing required audience configuration.

Numeric sentinel semantics for clock_skew_leeway: value 0 does NOT mean strict zero leeway; it selects the default 60 seconds. Value -1 disables this extra leeway. Never assume 0 disables skew tolerance.

Numeric sentinel semantics for expiration_leeway: value 0 does NOT mean strict zero leeway; it selects the default 150 seconds. Value -1 disables this extra leeway. For I2 expired_token tests, do not use 0 when you intend strict expiration enforcement.

Numeric sentinel semantics for not_before_leeway: value 0 does NOT mean strict zero leeway; it selects the default 150 seconds. Value -1 disables this extra leeway. For I2 future_token tests, do not use 0 when you intend strict nbf enforcement.

Parameter matching semantics: bound_subject supports exact string match only. There is no companion type parameter. Wildcards like '*' are treated literally. For I4 multi-identity tests, OMIT bound_subject entirely rather than setting it to a wildcard.

Parameter matching semantics: bound_audiences is exact list-membership matching only. There is no companion type parameter. Wildcards like '*' are treated literally. For I5 audience tests, configure explicit audience values; for multi-identity scenarios do not try to generalize with wildcard audiences.

Parameter matching semantics: user_claim is an exact claim-name selector, not a pattern. If user_claim_json_pointer=false, the value is treated as a literal claim name; if true, it is treated as a JSON pointer path. Do not use wildcard claim names in I4 tests.

Parameter matching semantics: groups_claim is an exact claim-name or JSON-pointer selector for a list-of-strings claim. There is no wildcard matching mode for the claim name itself. For I4/I5 group tests, vary the claim value, not the groups_claim parameter.

Parameter matching semantics: bound_claims defaults to exact literal matching because bound_claims_type defaults to 'string'. In this mode, '*' is a literal asterisk, not a wildcard. For I4 multi-identity scenarios that need multiple different values to pass the same role, either set bound_claims_type='glob' intentionally or omit the relevant bound_claims entry entirely.

Claim value type semantics: bound_claims accepts expected values as string, integer, boolean, or list of strings. When bound_claims_type='string' (default), values are treated as literals and must match exactly. For I5 numeric coercion tests, set bound_claims_type to 'glob' rather than the default 'string' so numeric claim values are coerced to strings instead of being rejected outright.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests against JWT login, include a control login using a valid token alongside the attack token. Recommended control claims: exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}}, iat={{now_epoch}}, sub={{jwt_sub}}. Without a control, LOGIN_FAILED may reflect broken trust/configuration rather than freshness enforcement.

Session-use budget: token_num_uses limits every API call made with the resulting Vault session token, including verify_granted_identity and verify_read_secret. If the sequence performs both self-lookup and secret-read verification, the minimum safe token_num_uses is 2; use 3+ if any additional session-authenticated call is inserted.
For I3 jwt_signing_key_rotation tests, update configure_jwt_validation so the old trust anchor is removed, then retry the SAME JWT. Leaving both old and new keys trusted is not a valid rotation test.

For I3 jwt_bound_issuer_enforce tests, bound_issuer is optional globally. If omitted, Vault skips issuer comparison entirely. The fuzzer MUST set bound_issuer in configure_jwt_validation before testing issuer enforcement or trust-anchor substitution.

For I1 alg_none and resign_attacker_key tests, jwt_supported_algs constrains accepted algorithms. If you narrow this list incorrectly, failures may be caused by algorithm allowlisting rather than signature/trust validation. Keep the baseline algorithm allowed while changing only the attack dimension under test.

For I3 jwt_default_role_change tests, login_with_jwt may omit role and then uses the mount's default_role. To test default-role coherence, the attack and control logins must both omit role explicitly; supplying role bypasses the default-role behavior entirely.

OIDC auth_url and callback are a session-bound pair. The callback requires the exact state and nonce from the preceding auth_url response, and optional client_nonce must match across both calls. For I3 flow-coherence tests, do not mix state/nonce/client_nonce values across sessions except when intentionally testing swap behavior.

OIDC role setup requires allowed_redirect_uris. The callback redirect_uri used in the upstream provider flow must be one of the role's allowed_redirect_uris. A mismatch is expected rejection, not an I3 bug.

Vault's OIDC auth_url endpoint returns a Vault-generated upstream authorization URL; it is not the upstream provider authorize endpoint itself. For OIDC-flow tests on the auth method, start_oidc_auth must call /v1/auth/{mount}/oidc/auth_url, then follow the returned auth_url externally, then complete /v1/auth/{mount}/oidc/callback.

For OIDC provider client setup, confidential clients may use client_secret_basic or client_secret_post and PKCE is optional; public clients use auth method 'none' and PKCE is required. When testing code exchange behavior, choose client_type deliberately or failures may be due to documented client authentication rules rather than a security flaw.

OIDC provider assignments default to allowing no Vault entities. To let identities authenticate through a provider client in tests, configure assignments explicitly or use the built-in allow_all assignment. Otherwise authorization failures are expected setup failures, not I5 violations.

OIDC provider allowed_client_ids default to allowing no clients when empty; '*' allows all clients. For provider-side token/userinfo tests, ensure the provider permits the client_id under test or the flow will fail by design.

The reserved OIDC scope name 'openid' cannot be created as a custom scope and is automatically required/included where applicable. Do not attempt to create a custom scope named openid as part of test setup.

KV v2 uses /data/ for secret reads and writes. If the target secret engine is version 2, verify_read_secret and seed_protected_resource must use /v1/{engine}/data/{path}; using /v1/{engine}/{path} will hit the wrong API shape and produce false 404/permission results.

KV v2 list operations require permissions on the /metadata/ path even if normal reads/writes use /data/. If a test needs to enumerate keys, grant list capability on /metadata/ explicitly; otherwise list failures are by design.

KV v2 config sentinel semantics: max_versions=0 does NOT mean keep zero versions; it means use the default retention of 10 versions. delete_version_after='0s' means no automatic timed deletion. Never interpret 0 as immediate deletion or zero retention.

Group policy application mode affects whether identity group policies apply only within namespace hierarchy or across any namespace. In Enterprise, if /sys/config/group-policy-application is set to 'any', cross-namespace group-derived policies are by design and must not be flagged as I5 escalation without accounting for this global setting.
